data.title: Robot Consulting Announces Receipt of Nasdaq Delisting Determination and Request to Appeal such Determination Before a Hearings Panel
data.description:
TOKYO, JP / ACCESS Newswire / October 24, 2026 / Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. ("Robot Consulting" or the "Company"), a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions and legal technology, announced it has received a delisting determination from the Listing Qualifications Department (the "Staff") of The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC ("Nasdaq") notifying the Company of the Staff's determination to delist the Company's American Depository Shares ("ADSs") pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rules 5101 and IM-5101-4.

The Staff's determination is based on concerns regarding historical trading activity in the Company's securities and Nasdaq's belief that certain factors may have made the Company's securities susceptible to manipulation by third parties.

Nasdaq Listing Rule IM-5101-4 allows Nasdaq "to exercise discretion to delist a company from Nasdaq based on the potential for one or more third parties to engage in misconduct impacting a company's securities where the [U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission] has implemented a temporary trading suspension." Nasdaq has articulated its belief that the ability for third parties to manipulate a security's price indicates that the security does not have sufficient liquidity to promote fair and orderly markets and, therefore, delisting is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest.

The Company has appealed the Staff's determination to a Hearings Panel (the "Panel") on October 23, 2026. As a result of the appeal, the suspension of the Company's securities and the filing of the Form 25-NSE by Nasdaq with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") will be stayed pending the Panel's review and decision, although the existing trading halt will remain in effect unless and until it has been lifted by Nasdaq.

To date, Nasdaq has not claimed or communicated a view that there has been any wrongdoing by the Company, whether in regard to Nasdaq's investigation of the recent trading activity of the Company's securities or otherwise. The delisting determination does not have any immediate effect on the Company's ongoing business operations or financial condition, and the Company will continue to conduct its business in the ordinary course.

About Robot Consulting Co., Ltd.

Robot Consulting Co., Ltd. is a Japanese platform service provider focusing on human resource solutions with an intention to expand into legal technology. The Company's major product, "Labor Robot," is a cloud-based human resource management system that helps users track employee attendance, manage sales orders, and journalize accounting items. Robot Consulting also assists users with grant and subsidy applications and provides consulting and support services for digital transformation to small and medium-sized businesses. Robot Consulting also aims to create more software and services related to digital transformation and legal technology. The Company has launched "Robot Lawyer," a platform that provides preliminary legal consultation resources to individuals and small businesses, particularly with respect to defamatory online posts or other reputational harm. For more information, visit www.robotconsulting.net.

data.title: Suspect arrested as fire engulfs Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest', German police say
data.description:
German police said they had detained a suspect after fire broke out at a historic mountain guest house known as the "Eagle's Nest", used as a retreat by Nazi officials, including the dictator Adolf Hitler.

Around 200 firefighters and emergency personnel in the area around Berchtesgaden in the southern region of Bavaria were battling the flames after the building, known as the Kehlsteinhaus, caught fire on Friday, police said.

Police are investigating whether the suspect, who was detained close to the scene, was connected to the fire, they said in a statement.

There was no immediate word about a possible motive.

Built in 1938 as a guest house for Nazi officials and their guests, the building, in a spectacular Alpine setting, is separate from Hitler's nearby summer residence, known as the Berghof.

Now owned by the state of Bavaria, the Kehlsteinhaus was classified after the war as a historical monument recalling the Nazi period.

data.title: Wall Street closes lower to end rocky week
data.description:
Wall Street's main ​indexes closed lower on Friday even as technology shares steadied somewhat to end a turbulent week for the market-driving AI trade, ‌and investors looked ahead to a busy slate of corporate earnings and a Federal Reserve interest-rate policy meeting.

The Nasdaq Composite posted a slim loss a day after the tech-heavy index suffered its biggest one-day drop since June, as concerns flared over financing costs to support heavy AI investment spending. The S&P 500 technology sector posted a 0.35% gain on Friday.

Most ​S&P 500 sectors fell, however, including declines of well over 1% for the consumer staples and consumer discretionary groups as well as the ​financials sector.

Next week, about one-third of S&P 500 companies report quarterly results, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, three AI hyperscalers whose ⁠capital spending forecasts will be closely watched on Wall Street.

"There is still fallout from the questioning of the AI trade," said Kristina Hooper, chief market ​strategist at Man Group. "There's certainly the potential that we see less invested in an AI data center build-out next year than has been projected. So I certainly ​think that's giving pause."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16; the S&P 500 lost 39.75 points, or 0.52%, to 7,623.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 53.52 points, or 0.21%, to 25,955.34.

For the week, the S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq dropped 0.7%. The blue-chip Dow rose 0.4%, its third straight weekly gain.

Telecommunications stocks fell, ​weighing on the communication services sector, after a report that SpaceX was seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier.

Shares of AT&T and ​T-Mobile both sank nearly 8% while Verizon shed 1.2%. SpaceX shares rose 1.9%. US cell tower operators gained, with Crown Castle up 9% and American Tower up 4%.

The energy ‌sector rose ⁠2.5%, hitting a record high. Brent crude hit its highest level since late April, after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concern over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East.

American Express shares fell 3.7%, weighing on the Dow. The company raised its profit forecast as it also announced plans to eliminate 5% of its workforce.

SLB shares rose 7% after the oilfield services provider beat Wall Street estimates for third-quarter profit.

Data from the University of Michigan showed US consumer sentiment edged ​down near a record low in ​October, as rising prices because of ⁠the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy.

Market focus remains on the earnings season, with robust corporate profit growth underpinning gains for major equity indexes this year. S&P 500 companies are on track to have increased earnings ​by more than 32% in the third quarter, according to LSEG IBES data.

The Fed is expected to keep interest ​rates steady when it ⁠gives its policy statement on Wednesday, but investors will be eager for clues about whether the US central bank will hike rates at its December meeting. Wall Street is also increasingly focused on the November 3 midterm elections, which will decide control of the US Congress.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.72-to-1 ratio on the New ⁠York Stock ​Exchange. On the Nasdaq, declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 1.57-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted ​18 new 52-week highs and 8 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 74 new highs and 334 new lows.

Volume on US exchanges was 15.4 billion shares, compared with the 17.2 billion ​average over the last 20 trading days.

data.title: Azerbaijan sees ties with India moving to "higher levels"
data.description:
Baku, Oct. 23 -- Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Jeyhun Bayramov expressed confidence on Friday that bilateral relations with India are progressing towards higher levels, noting expanding prospects across energy sectors, pharmaceuticals, agriculture and logistical corridors, while characterising External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar's official visit to Baku as "a very valuable meeting".

Following his meeting with EAM Jaishankar in the Azerbaijani capital, Bayramov described the exchange as comprehensive, constructive and highly productive, addressing various bilateral, regional and global issues.

Bayramov noted that this diplomatic engagement served as a logical continuation of previous high-level interactions between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Summit held in Bishkek last month.

Emphasising commercial relations, the top Azerbaijani diplomat stated that bilateral trade volume had reached approximately USD 600 million this year, though he acknowledged that this figure remained below the true economic capacity of both nations. The minister underscored that India's ONGC had enhanced its stake in a major oil and gas project within Azerbaijan, alongside more than 1,000 Indian corporate entities currently active in the country.

Furthermore, Bayramov pointed to energy, agricultural cooperation and pharmaceutical collaboration as key growth areas, alongside major transit networks connecting eastern, western, northern and southern corridors, leveraging Azerbaijan's strategic geographical location.

Concerning cultural and interpersonal connections, Bayramov reported that two direct flight routes operated between Baku and Delhi, approximately 500 Indian scholars had enrolled in Azerbaijani higher education institutions this year, and over 30 Indian cinematic productions had utilised local backdrops in recent years.

The two foreign ministers additionally evaluated geopolitical conditions within the South Caucasus, encompassing peace and normalisation efforts between Armenia and Azerbaijan, escalating frictions in the Middle East and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war, according to Bayramov.

"We believe that this visit and the discussions that we have had on the various issues will have a good impact on the development of the bilateral relationship between our two nations," Bayramov stated, according to the English translation of his remarks.

Earlier on Friday, EAM Jaishankar called on Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev in Baku, where both leaders held detailed discussions aimed at deepening cooperative frameworks between the two countries.

"Pleased to call on Ilham Aliyev of Azerbaijan in Baku this morning. Conveyed the greetings of President Droupadi Murmu and PM Modi. Discussed strengthening the relationship between our two countries. Appreciate his positive sentiments for this shared endeavour," EAM Jaishankar posted on X.

data.title: Infosys Growth Outlook Sours Despite Strong Deal Wins
data.description:
Revenue growth guidance narrowed to 1 to 2 per cent despite USD 5.2 billion in Q2 deal wins; net profit misses analyst estimates as US-listed shares fall

Infosys cut its FY27 revenue growth forecast on Friday as weakness in its largest market, North America, weighed on its outlook, despite stronger deal bookings. Net profit for the September quarter rose 6.2 per cent year-on-year (YoY) but fell short of analyst estimates, while the revised guidance sent its US-listed shares lower in premarket trading.

The Bengaluru-based IT services major lowered its constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1 to 2 per cent for FY27 from 1.5 to 3 per cent previously, signalling continued pressure on near-term growth. The revision came even as large-deal total contract value (TCV) increased to USD 5.2 billion in the quarter from USD 3.1 billion a year earlier, with 62 per cent of the deal value classified as net new business.

North America Weakness Weighs On Outlook

Revenue from North America, which accounts for more than half of Infosys’ sales, declined 1.5 per cent YoY in constant-currency terms in the September quarter, marking the region’s weakest performance in two years. The company cited softer demand, with high-technology and retail clients in the region scaling down projects.

Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said the quarter had been softer, with pricing pressure arising from intense competition and clients seeking to capture productivity gains from artificial intelligence (AI). These factors were reflected in the revised growth guidance, he said during the company’s earnings call.

Deal Bookings Rise As Revenue Outlook Weakens

Infosys reported large-deal TCV of USD 5.2 billion in Q2, up from USD 3.1 billion in the year-ago quarter and USD 3.6 billion in the preceding quarter. Of the total deal value, 62 per cent came from net-new business.

However, the stronger bookings did not prevent Infosys from lowering its full-year growth forecast. Contract wins represent the value of business secured, while the revenue contribution depends on project commencement, execution and the recognition of services over time. The revised guidance points to limited confidence in a stronger near-term growth trajectory, even as the company continues to win large transformation engagements. Infosys retained its FY27 operating-margin guidance at 20 to 22 per cent.

Infosys reported consolidated net profit of Rs 7,823 crore for the September quarter, up 6.2 per cent from Rs 7,364 crore a year earlier. The figure was below the analyst estimates. Revenue rose 10.7 per cent YoY to Rs 49,244 crore. In constant-currency terms, revenue grew 1.5 per cent YoY and 1.2 per cent sequentially, while operating margin remained stable at 21 per cent.

The company’s US-listed shares fell 7.5 per cent in premarket trading. The market reaction followed the lower growth forecast amid continued weakness in North America and a profit figure below analyst expectations.

AI Revenue Grows Amid Pricing Pressure

AI-related revenue accounted for 10.5 per cent of Infosys’ total revenue in Q2 and grew 29 per cent sequentially, the company said. Chief Executive Officer Salil Parekh said the company was seeing growing demand for AI-related work as enterprises moved towards adoption at scale.

“Worldwide spending on AI services is forecast to reach USD 1.3 trillion by 2030 as enterprise buyers demand efficient, automated service delivery,” said Shubham Singh Rathore, principal analyst at Gartner.

The growth in AI revenue, however, has yet to change the company’s overall revenue outlook. Infosys is navigating a market in which AI is creating new technology-services opportunities while also increasing pressure on traditional work through productivity demands and pricing competition.

For FY27, the company maintained its operating-margin guidance at 20 to 22 per cent while lowering its revenue growth forecast. The pace at which large-deal wins translate into recognised revenue, alongside a recovery in North American demand, will remain important to its growth trajectory.

data.title: AI Automation Can Lift Margins Despite Pricing Pressure: Coforge CEO
data.description:
CEO Sudhir Singh says AI is changing the economics of IT services as record deal wins, faster contract ramp-ups and efficiency gains shape the company's growth strategy

Coforge is betting on proactive, client-specific solutions and artificial intelligence (AI)-led efficiencies to sustain growth and protect margins as automation reshapes the economics of the IT services industry. The company is seeking to move beyond conventional, effort-based technology contracts towards engagements centred on enterprise transformation and business outcomes.

“AI is breaking the link between scale and margin leadership for the tech services industry,” Chief Executive Officer Sudhir Singh said during the company's Q2 FY27 earnings call. He said automation across delivery and internal functions could help improve profitability even as pricing pressure intensifies.

Coforge reported order intake of USD 1.04 billion in the September quarter, exceeding USD 1 billion for the second time in its history. It also signed eight large deals, the highest number in a single quarter for the company, while organic constant-currency revenue grew 3.8 per cent sequentially and its reported EBIT margin stood at 16 per cent.

Singh said most of the recently signed contracts would begin ramping up relatively quickly, supporting the company's growth outlook. “The ramp-ups will be near immediate in most cases, and growth outlook continues to be very robust,” he said.

Moving Beyond Price Competition

Singh said most of Coforge's large deals were sole-sourced and driven by proactive solutions. Rather than offering standardised platforms or competing primarily on price, the company is seeking to develop offerings suited to individual clients' operating environments and business requirements.

“The only way to sustain both growth and margin simultaneously is to make sure that we lead with proactive solutions through an exceptional solutioning on-site engine that we have, and close deals without getting into fisticuffs with other providers around pricing,” Singh said.

The approach reflects a broader shift in how the company wants to position itself as AI changes the economics of technology services. Traditional time-and-material contracts link revenue closely to the effort deployed, while automation can reduce the labour required to deliver technology projects. Coforge is seeking to differentiate its proposals through domain expertise, AI-led efficiency and solutions designed around specific business outcomes.

John Speight, President and Executive Director at Coforge, said the company's proactive proposal approach was also changing its conversations with clients. He described the shift as “a significant move away from a cost play to a value play”, with AI-led efficiency and business outcomes becoming central to its approach.

The company has also started securing deals through advisory channels that it had not traditionally accessed, Speight said. This adds another route to business alongside its efforts to develop client-specific solutions as procurement-driven requests for proposals slow.

AI And The Margin Equation

Coforge's strategy also depends on using AI to improve its own operating efficiency. Singh said the company had been investing significantly in its AI initiatives, including Momentum Blue, its forward-deployed engineering model, which places engineers alongside client teams to develop solutions in their business context.

Coforge raised its FY27 consolidated EBIT margin guidance to 16 per cent from 15.5 per cent. Chief Financial Officer Saurabh Goyal said AI-led efficiencies in fixed-price contracts would start reflecting in Q4 margin numbers. He added that AI-led efficiencies across general and administrative functions would support further productivity gains and incremental margin benefits.

The company is also seeking to improve utilisation and benefit from operating leverage as it scales. Singh said its margin ambitions would not come at the expense of growth. “We continue to be the firm that prioritizes growth over everything else,” he said, adding that AI presented an opportunity to separate margin performance from the scale of a technology services business.

Healthcare Adds Growth Momentum

Coforge's changing business mix provides further context for its growth strategy. According to Gaurav Vasu, CEO and Founder of UnearthInsight, Healthcare and HiTech together accounted for 17.6 per cent of revenue, up from 10 per cent a year earlier. The combined segment grew 13.7 per cent sequentially in constant-currency terms.

Banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI and Insurance), meanwhile, accounted for a smaller share of revenue than a year earlier despite growing in absolute terms. The shift indicates that faster growth in Healthcare and HiTech is reshaping Coforge's revenue mix, although the combined reporting category does not reveal the individual contribution of each vertical.

Encora Adds To Pipeline

The Encora acquisition is providing additional opportunities to combine capabilities across the two businesses. Singh said the acquired company's revenue growth was expected to move in line with Coforge's from Q3 onwards, following a largely flat revenue performance in the first full quarter after the acquisition.

The largest deal in the company's current pipeline involved an Encora client, while Coforge's largest healthcare account had also come from the acquired business. Management did not disclose the value or scope of the prospective contract.

Singh said the integration was helping the company cross-sell capabilities across clients, while the acquired business's margin expansion was ahead of the acquisition plan.

Coforge's ability to sustain growth will depend on converting its deal pipeline into revenue while using AI to improve delivery efficiency and protect profitability. The coming quarters will show whether faster contract ramp-ups and a changing business mix can support growth alongside the company's margin ambitions.

data.title: Junshi Biosciences Announces Completion of First Patient Dosing in the Phase 3 Clinical Trial of JS203 in Combination with Chemotherapy for the Treatment of Diffuse Large B-cell Lymphoma
data.description:
SHANGHAI, China, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Shanghai Junshi Biosciences Co., Ltd (“Junshi Biosciences,” HKEX: 1877; SSE: 688180), a leading innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the discovery, development, and commercialization of novel therapies, announced that the first patient dosing has been completed in a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 3 clinical study of the company’s product, a recombinant humanized anti-CD20/CD3 bispecific antibody code:JS203, in combination with chemotherapy compared to rituximab in combination with chemotherapy in patients with relapsed/refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (R/R DLBCL) (the JS203-003-III-DLBCL Study; NCT07808827). This study is the first registrational clinical study for JS203.

DLBCL is one of the most common types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL), accounting for approximately 40% of adult NHL cases in China. According to GLOBOCAN 2022 statistics, there are approximately 45,000 new cases of DLBCL in China each year, and the incidence rate shows a slow increasing trend. DLBCL is characterized by high aggressiveness and rapid progression. A retrospective study in an Asian population showed that, even after active treatment, patients with relapsed or refractory DLBCL had a median overall survival (mOS) of over one year and a 5-year survival rate of approximately 30%, which necessitates the exploration of more proactive and effective treatment options.

JS203 is a recombinant humanized anti-CD20/CD3 bispecific antibody self-developed by Junshi Biosciences. It consists of anti-CD20 segment and anti-CD3 segment. By associating and activating lymphoma cells (binding to CD20) and T cells (binding to CD3), JS203 can enable T cells to kill lymphoma cells effectively.

Results from a phase 1 clinical study showed that, for JS203 monotherapy at the recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) administered with step-up dosing (SUD) to 30 mg for the treatment of patients with CD20-positive relapsed or refractory B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, the objective response rate (ORR) reached 72.4%. Among patients with DLBCL, the ORR was 69.7%, and the complete response rate CRR was 39.4%, with persistent relief observed. Meanwhile, the overall safety profile was manageable, with a cytokine release syndrome (CRS) incidence rate of only 27.3% and no occurrence of immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS).

The JS203-003-III-DLBCL Study is a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 3 clinical trial, with Professor Yuqin SONG of Beijing Cancer Hospital serving as the principal investigator. It aims to compare the efficacy and safety of JS203 in combination with chemotherapy compared to rituximab in combination with chemotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. The study plans to enroll 282 subjects, with overall survival (OS) as its primary endpoint. This study is the first registrational clinical study for JS203.

The JS203-003-III-DLBCL study team commented: “Early clinical studies have shown encouraging efficacy and a favorable safety profile for JS203 in combination with chemotherapy in patients with R/R DLBCL, reinforcing our confidence in the ongoing Phase 3 study. We are committed to advancing the study with rigor and efficiency, with the aim of making a new treatment option available to patients as soon as possible.”

About JS203

JS203 is a recombinant humanized anti-CD20/CD3 bispecific antibody self-developed by Junshi Biosciences. CD20 is a B lymphocyte restricted differentiation antigen and one of the most successful targets for B-cell lymphoma treatment. CD3 is an important marker on the surface of T cells, and the main mechanism of T cell engaging bispecific antibodies is using CD3 as a mediator to activate T cells to specifically attack tumor cells. JS203 consists of anti-CD20 segment and anti-CD3 segment. By associating and activating lymphoma cells (binding to CD20) and T cells (binding to CD3), JS203 can enable T cells to kill lymphoma cells effectively. To date, a Phase 3 clinical study evaluating JS203 in combination with chemotherapy versus rituximab in combination with chemotherapy in patients with relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (R/R DLBCL) is ongoing.

About Junshi Biosciences

Founded in December 2012, Junshi Biosciences (HKEX: 1877; SSE: 688180) is an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company dedicated to the discovery, development and commercialization of innovative therapeutics. With our outstanding capacity for innovative drug discovery, strong biotechnology R&D capability, and large-scale production capacity, we have successfully developed a drug candidate portfolio with global competitiveness and a well-structured research pipeline, which covers therapeutic areas including cancer, autoimmune, metabolic, and infectious diseases. Our innovative field spans cutting-edge therapeutic modalities, including mAbs, small-molecule drugs, ADCs, bsAb/msAb, fusion proteins, nucleic acid drugs and vaccines. Five of the company’s products have received marketing authorizations in China and international markets, one of which is toripalimab, China’s domestically developed anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody. Toripalimab has been approved in over 50 countries and regions including China, the US, and Europe.

With a mission of “providing patients with world-class, trustworthy, affordable, and innovative drugs,” Junshi Biosciences is “In China, For Global.” The company currently employs more than 3,000 people worldwide. Headquartered in Shanghai, China, it has a business presence in multiple countries and regions around the world. For more information, please visit: http://www.junshipharma.com.

data.title: Trinidad and Tobago in talks with ONGC Videsh, Oil India to refine Venezuelan crude
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Trinidad and Tobago is in talks with state-run ONGC Videsh Ltd (OVL) and Oil India Ltd on a proposal to process Venezuelan crude at its Guaracara refinery, which is being reopened after remaining shut for more than seven years, the nation's high commissioner to India, Chandradath Singh, said in an interview.

The Caribbean government has proposed that the two Indian oil companies process crude from neighbouring Venezuela at the Guaracara refinery in Pointe-a-Pierre, which forms part of the former Petrotrin complex and is currently under renovation, Singh said. Guaracara Refining Company, a subsidiary of Trinidad Petroleum Holdings, manages the refinery.

"I am having discussions with them. They are very interested. They have oil wells in Venezuela, which are now opening up. We have the biggest refinery in the entire region, in Trinidad and Tobago, which was shut down for a while. But we are now reopening it," Singh told Mint.

The proposal comes as India scouts for energy supplies from across the world amid turmoil in global energy markets triggered by the war in West Asia. India imports about 90% of its annual crude oil requirement from around 41 countries. The market remains volatile, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel amid renewed shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz.

The proposal "could widen India's energy partnership amid instability in the global oil market," said Anisur Rahman, professor at the centre for West Asia studies at Jamia Millia Islamia University.

India's imports of Venezuelan oil have also increased. According to S&P Global, daily volumes of Venezuelan oil supplied to India averaged about 190,000 barrels a day in 2026,'' he added.

"Such a measure may help Trinidad restore its economy, while the feasibility of the proposal depends on the compatibility of the facilities for processing the oil, transportation costs, the discount on the crude, financing and the sanctions in place," he added.

The proposal comes as US secretary of state Marco Rubio, during his recent visit to India, said Reliance Industries Ltd, which operates the world's largest integrated refinery complex in Jamnagar, Gujarat, has the capacity to process more heavy Venezuelan crude.

"They have the capability to refine heavy crude. They've done so in the past, and I think as more and more Venezuelan oil comes online, it's something they can do," he said.

The US has been pushing India to buy more Venezuelan oil following the change of government in the South American nation and the US takeover of control of its oil and gas assets.

The refinery has a capacity of 165,000 barrels per day (bpd) and has been shut since November 2018 because of losses and high debt. The Caribbean country announced plans to reopen it this year.

In January, Trinidad and Tobago's energy minister, Roodal Moonilal, said the government was in talks with state-run Indian Oil Corp. Ltd (IOC) to restart the refinery as the country sought to revive refining capacity that had been shut for more than seven years.

The Guaracara refinery previously processed crude from Venezuela, as well as supplies from Africa and Russia. Trinidad and Tobago's domestic crude production is below 55,000 bpd, according to the country's energy ministry.

OVL, the overseas arm of Oil and Natural Gas Corp. Ltd (ONGC), has held a 40% stake in Venezuela's San Cristobal oilfield since 2008, with state-owned Petróleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA) holding the remaining stake. US sanctions squeezed production at San Cristobal and halted the repatriation of dividends from the businesses. Separately, OVL partnered with IOC and Oil India to invest $2.2 billion in the Carabobo-1 project.

"The companies will have to analyse the proposal and look into its economic viability," said another official familiar with the developments.

At the time of writing, the December contract on the Intercontinental Exchange was trading at $114.30 a barrel, up 0.98% from its previous close. The International Energy Agency expects global oil supply to remain in deficit through the end of the year as the recovery in Middle Eastern exports remains fragile.

The proposal and the discussions follow the US Office of Foreign Assets Control (Ofac) granting a general license in July for OVL's partnerships in Venezuela.

In a filing with the BSE on 18 August, ONGC said, "The required go-ahead was received from US government in July, 2026. Framework agreements for further course of action in both the assets are under discussion with relevant stakeholders."

Addressing reporters in September after ONGC's annual general meeting, OVL managing director Rajarshi Gupta said the framework for further operations could be completed within the next three months.

Mint previously reported that OVL was in talks with PDVSA and Venezuela's new government on the mode of payment-cash or oil in lieu of cash. OVL has also sought operatorship of the San Cristobal oilfield.

The company was expected to receive dividends during a six-month US sanctions waiver on Venezuela that began in October 2023. However, it failed to receive the cargo during that period, and the plan stalled when sanctions were reimposed.

Venezuela, which has the world's largest oil reserves, has been under US sanctions since 2015. On 3 January 2026, the US captured President Nicolas Maduro and his wife in Caracas and flew them to the US. US President Donald Trump later signed an executive order declaring a national emergency to protect Venezuelan oil revenues held in US Treasury accounts from attachment or judicial process. Sanctions on Venezuela were lifted shortly afterwards, reopening oil flows. In August, Venezuela was India's fourth-largest crude supplier, with shipments of 383,000 bpd.

India imported $3.04 billion worth of crude oil from Venezuela in April-July of fiscal year 2027 (FY27), up 1,092% from $255.27 million in the corresponding period of FY26. In FY26, crude oil imports from Venezuela were valued at $255.27 million, down 81.85% from $1.40 billion in FY25, according to data from the Union ministry of commerce and industry.

Queries emailed to Trinidad and Tobago's ministry of energy and energy industries, ONGC, Oil India, India's ministry of external affairs, the ministry of petroleum and natural gas, and the chairman of Guaracara Refining Company remained unanswered at press time.
